localBiteReport: The most recent available reports covering Choctawhatchee Bay are from the week of September 4–10, 2026 (published September 3), plus a local angler report from approximately September 10. Water temperature at this location is 87°F. Guides and local anglers are noting the first signs of the fall transition — bait schools are moving from open water onto flats, bayous, and roll-downs, and the bite overall is picking up. Redfish are the standout inshore story right now: a Santa Rosa Beach angler reported a 40¼-inch, 26-lb bull redfish this past week, and sight-fishing opportunities for slot reds on the flats are described as improving. Speckled trout are also showing well, with one local angler noting there have been a lot of them including some quality fish. Early morning remains the prime window for both species given the heat, with midday typically slow.
